answer: An agent economy can weight voting and task allocation by slashable collateral rather than by account count: each agent must lock a fixed bond before joining, and a randomly selected audit checks whether its work is valid. Creating a hundred identities then requires a hundred bonds, while detected fraud burns them, so splitting one stake cannot multiply influence. The pulse of new tasks may trigger a spiral of audits through a grove of agents, making mass fake identities costly to fund and risky to operate.
